items.title: Warren Buffett Finished Buying Coca-Cola in August 1994 and Never Bought Another Share. Under Greg Abel, Berkshire Now Collects $2.3 Million a Day From It
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway's 400 million Coca-Cola shares, bought for $1,299 million between 1988 and 1994 and never added to since, now pay $848 million a year, about $2.3 million a day. Computed from Coca-Cola's split-adjusted dividend history, the checks since 1994 add up to about $13 billion, ten times the cost, and the next $212 million payment is due December 15.

items.title: Anthropic falls below IPO price as Nvidia gives back gains
items.summary: In this edition of Sozzi Unleashed: At The Close, Brian Sozzi sorts through "reality trading" as Nvidia slides nearly 7% after Monday's 31% surge and Anthropic falls below its $83 IPO price less than a week after the biggest offering in history. GCG Advisory Partners' Bill Gunderson makes the case that Nvidia is the cheapest growth stock in the market at nine times forward earnings and names Nvidia and Eli Lilly as his top picks for 2027. Brian breaks down Dell's blowout quarter and $132 billion AI backlog, and HPE CEO Antonio Neri joins to explain the company's raised outlook, why it refuses to finance neoclouds, and whether server margins have peaked. Brian closes by arguing the AI trade is reaching consumers' wallets, pointing to Best Buy's strongest comparable sales growth in five years.

items.title: Coca-Cola hires pharma vet for CFO
items.summary: The beverage giant is breaking from its typical practice of appointing insiders by naming pharma finance alum David Elkins as its incoming CFO, analysts noted.

items.title: Short-Term Bond Funds vs. Dividend Stocks: Which Income Holds Up Better for Retirees?
items.summary: Treasury bills out-yield Exxon and Coca-Cola today, but that paycheck resets with every Fed move while dividends answer to a board. Before choosing, retirees should weigh what each income stream can lose, and what the tax code lets them keep.
